subject: Redwood Dedicated RFI — GPU mix, throughput targets, reservation cadence
messages:
From: Jordan Hale <jordan.hale@gridlytics.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@gridlytics.com
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI — Dedicated capacity: throughput targets, GPU candidates, reservation cadence

Avery — thanks for taking our RFI. We've attached a short demand profile and a list of workload types. High level asks:
- Target 99th p99 latency <= 450ms for 1k qps of short-text generation (avg 60 tokens)
- Batch embedding throughput target: 150k embeddings/day (batchable)
- We want a recommended GPU mix and an initial monthly commitment profile for 6/12/24 month options

Can you confirm which GPU SKUs you recommend for this workload and how Redwood calculates headroom/burst slots? Also, include any suggested quantization options for reducing unit cost while preserving our hallucination tolerances.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Hale | Director, Platform Engineering
GridLytics
Attachments: GridLytics_Demand_Profile.csv

From: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Hale <jordan.hale@gridlytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI — Dedicated capacity: throughput targets, GPU candidates, reservation cadence

Jordan — appreciate the detailed profile, this is very helpful. Quick summary of what we'll deliver in the formal RFI packet (attached): recommended GPU SKUs and expected throughput per SKU, latency projections at p50/p95/p99 for your short-text generation profile, batch embedding throughput estimates, and a suggested 3-tier reservation cadence (baseline, seasonal burst, emergency overflow).

Key clarifications we need before finalizing numbers:
- For the 1k qps gen target, is the token distribution skewed (many short requests + occasional long ones) or broadly consistent? The KV cache hit-rate assumption changes packing and slot counts.
- For embeddings: are the 150k/day all offline/batched (within 1–2 hour windows) or spread across the day?

I'll loop in Ben (account) for commercial phasing and Karthik + Soojin for engineering fitment. I'm attaching an initial SKU/pricing sheet and a phasing workbook so you can poke at the numbers.

Next step: if you can reply with the two clarifications above, we'll produce a finalized reservation recommendation and the SLA carveouts for burst lanes.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference runtime
Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_SKUs_and_Pricing.pdf, commitment-phasing-proposal-v1.xlsx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: sizing notes for GridLytics RFI (do not forward)

Avery/Ben — quick internal notes after looking at GridLytics_Demand_Profile.csv:
- The 1k qps short-text profile is heavy on 8–70 token responses (~78% under 100 tokens) with a 4% tail >512 tokens. Treat as skewed small-requests workload; recommend prioritizing low-latency SKUs and aggressive prefix caching.
- GPU fitment: propose a blended pool of A100-80GB (quant-friendly FP16 path) for latency-critical short-text and H100-80GB for throughput-heavy batched embedding runs. Also recommend adding a small percentage (10–12%) of Q/A-optimized Ampere-variant instances to reduce cold-starts for LLMs with wide attention patterns.
- Throughput math (rough): one A100-80GB slot @ p99 ~410ms for 1k qps with 20% KV cache hit-rate, so plan for 1.25x baseline slots to hit p99 headroom. For embedding batches: H100 pool can handle a 24k-35k embeddings/hour window depending on batch size — recommend evening windows for cost efficiency.
- Burst strategy: create two burst lanes — reserved burst (prepaid additional slots you can draw on) and ephemeral overflow (hosted, pay-as-you-go, lower priority). We'll specify routing fallback: reserved -> ephemeral -> hosted public fallback.

Questions for commercial: what commitment term mix are we comfortable guaranteeing for burst SLA? Ben, need your input on pricing slabs in the phasing workbook before we send to GridLytics.

- Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Hale <jordan.hale@gridlytics.com>, procurement@gridlytics.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Final RFI packet: recommended GPU mix, reservation cadence, and SLOs (GridLytics)

Jordan / Procurement team — attaching the finalized recommendation based on your demand profile and our internal sizing review. Highlights below, and the full workbook is attached: commitment-phasing-proposal-v1.xlsx

Executive summary:
- Recommended baseline: 12 A100-80GB slots dedicated to short-text generation (optimized FP16 path with KV cache). Expected p99 latency: ~410ms with 20% cache hit-rate; p95 ~220ms. Baseline includes a 25% headroom buffer for compaction and autoscale latency guardrails.
- Embeddings: 2 H100-80GB nodes in a dedicated batch pool for nightly windows (150k/day comfortably supported with batch sizes 512–2048). We recommend a scheduled 2–4 hour batch window to minimize costs.
- Commitment cadence options: 6/12/24 month tiers with stepped discounts. Suggested initial commitment: 60% of steady-state baseline for first 3 months (pilot), ramp to 100% by month 6. Burst lanes: 25% reserved burst (prepaid credits) + unlimited ephemeral overflow (best-effort).
- Quantization guidance: For short-text generation we recommend dynamic FP16 with 8-bit KV cache where acceptable — gives ~18–28% cost reduction in token compute with <1.5% impact on key-phrase hallucination tests (per our evals). We include a flagging policy — any generation with hallucination score over threshold routes to higher-precision lane.

Attachments included: Redwood_Dedicated_SKUs_and_Pricing.pdf, commitment-phasing-proposal-v1.xlsx (workbook with slot math and pricing lines).

Requested next steps:
1) Please confirm token length distribution and embedding batch window if our assumptions above are correct.
2) If acceptable, we'll prepare a draft MSA addendum with the commitment schedule and burst credit terms for legal review.
3) Schedule a 30-minute handoff call with Karthik & Soojin to walk through operational details (KV caching, autoscale thresholds, maintenance windows).

Thanks — happy to iterate on numbers if you want different tradeoffs (lower cost vs tighter p99).

Best,
Avery Johnson
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0197
Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_SKUs_and_Pricing.pdf, commitment-phasing-proposal-v1.xlsx
